Winds of Change: Facing the Twentieth Century.
When the twentieth century rolled in, it felt like the world outside Covert was picking up speed. Railroads seemed to reach farther every year, cities stretched higher into the sky, and the latest inventions promised to shake up everyday life. But with all that progress? New pressures crept in. Those old wounds across the country—especially when it came to race—were still wide open. And in a lot of places, the lines between people just got sharper instead of fading away.
Inside Covert, the unity that had carried the town for so long started facing some tough tests. Some families packed up and left, chasing factory jobs or the energy of big city living. At the same time, newcomers arrived, each bringing their own customs and fresh expectations. Even the schoolhouse, once the heart of togetherness, echoed with debates about what kids should learn and how discipline should work. The church, usually a steady comfort, now found itself wrestling with questions about what to hold onto—and what needed to change.
Picture this: one evening, a handful of longtime neighbors gathered on a front porch, watching the sun slip behind the trees. Their voices were soft as they talked over the changes they’d seen—the new faces, the new rhythms of work and worship. Some worried the old ways were slipping away for good. But others looked at the change and saw possibility, even hope, in the fresh energy and ideas streaming in.
There was a young teacher, brand new to Covert, who noticed tension in her classroom. Some kids clung to what they knew, while others wanted something different. She tried to bridge that gap, leaning on Covert’s history of working together. It wasn’t always simple. Some days, misunderstandings flared up, and old fears made themselves known. But most of the time, the kids found their way back to each other—maybe over a shared laugh, a group project, or just a game at recess.
The truth is, most people don’t realize just how fragile community really is, especially when everything around you seems to be changing overnight. In Covert, the real test was holding on to what truly mattered—kindness, fairness, and the belief that everyone belonged—while still making space for new voices and fresh ideas. It became clear that the work of building trust is never really finished. Every generation had to choose, again and again, to reach across those lines that threatened to split folks apart.
As the years rolled by, Covert’s story became both a comfort and a challenge. It reminded people of what’s possible, sure—but also just how much effort it takes to keep hope alive. The legacy of the town wasn’t some finished monument—it was a living promise. One that had to be renewed, over and over, with every act of courage, every moment of understanding, and every leap of faith.
